content.title: 7. Acute coronary syndrome with unstable presentation

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: ACS patients can present with haemodynamic compromise (e.g. out-of-hospital cardiac arrest [OHCA] and/or cardiogenic shock [CS]).

sections.heading: Antithrombotic therapy note (header context)
sections.text: For ACS not undergoing reperfusion, unless bleeding risk concerns prevail, a DAPT regimen based on clopidogrel and aspirin may provide net clinical benefit among older ACS patients. Further information is provided in the Supplementary data online.

sections.heading: 7.1 Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) in ACS
recommendations: Although a small minority of ACS present as OHCA, ACS is the most common cause of OHCA.
Resuscitation efforts in patients with OHCA should follow the European Resuscitation Council Guidelines.
Majority of adult cardiac arrest cases are associated with obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD); ACS should be included in the differential diagnosis.

Invasive coronary angiography (ICA) can be part of post-resuscitation management for patients estimated to have a high probability of acute coronary occlusion (e.g. persistent ST-segment elevation or equivalents and/or haemodynamic/electrical instability).
Neurological status (e.g. comatose vs non-comatose) and survival probability should be included in decision-making about invasive strategies.

sections.heading: Management of ROSC with ST-segment elevation
sections.text: Patients with return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) and persistent ST-segment elevation should generally undergo a PPCI strategy (immediate ICA and PCI if indicated), based on overall clinical situation and benefit/risk assessment. Registry reports associate emergent ICA and PCI with good outcomes, particularly in patients who are non-comatose at initial assessment.

sections.heading: Management of ROSC without ST-segment elevation
sections.text: Management should be individualized according to haemodynamic and neurological status. In OHCA with an initial shockable rhythm and without ST-segment elevation or cardiogenic shock, routine immediate ICA was not superior to a delayed invasive strategy in randomized trials (COACT and TOMAHAWK). Smaller underpowered trials (EMERGE, PEARL, COUPE) yielded similar findings.

Trials_and_studies_mentioned: COACT (Coronary Angiography after Cardiac Arrest) RCT
TOMAHAWK (Immediate Unselected Coronary Angiography Versus Delayed Triage in Survivors of Out-of-hospital Cardiac Arrest Without ST-segment Elevation) RCT
